ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows an AC source labeled Vm sin(ωt) feeding a phase-controlled rectifier block. On the rectifier DC side, the output voltage V0 is marked with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative. The load connected across this output is a series R-L-E load: a 2 Ω resistor, a 10 mH inductor, and an 80 V battery whose positive terminal is at the top. Reasoning: The battery is lossless, so the average battery power is P_batt = E I_avg. With P_batt = 1600 W and E = 80 V, I_avg = 1600/80 = 20 A. In steady state, the inductor has zero average voltage, so the average rectifier output voltage equals the battery voltage plus the average resistor drop: V0_avg = 80 + 2(20) = 120 V. The given expression is V0 = Vm/(2π)(3 + cos α), and Vm = 80π V, so V0 = (80π)/(2π)(3 + cos α) = 40(3 + cos α). Setting this equal to 120 gives 40(3 + cos α) = 120, so 3 + cos α = 3 and cos α = 0. In the usual firing-angle range, α = 90°.
